result:
Solution 3 gives the correct count, 7. This rests on my recollection that the known answer is 7, plus a check of its construction. I did not prove that no other rectangles are possible.

**Why Solution 1 is wrong.** Periodic staircase cuts can produce new rectangles, so the straight cut at the midpoint is not the only option. Its claim that no useful periodicity exists because gcd(2024, 2025) = 1 does not hold.

**Why Solution 2 is wrong.** The condition "divisor of the area in [1012, 2024]" is not justified. Divisibility of the area alone does not make a rectangle achievable, so the count of 21 has no valid basis.

**Checking Solution 3.** A periodic staircase cut lets one piece slide by one period to form a new rectangle. This gives two families.

- **Type A:** n divides 2024 and n−1 divides 2025. The divisors of 2025 give n−1 = 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 25, 27, 45, 75, 81, 135, 225, 405, 675, 2025, so n = 2, 4, 6, 10, 16, 26, 28, 46, 76, 82, 136, 226, 406, 676, 2026. Only n = 2, 4, 46 divide 2024. That gives 3 rectangles.
- **Type B:** m divides 2025 and m−1 divides 2024. The values m−1 = 2, 4, 8, 44, 2024 work, giving m = 3, 5, 9, 45, 2025. The case m = 2025 would need a 1-wide strip, but each piece has height about 2024, so it cannot form a 1 × 4,098,600 rectangle. That leaves 4 rectangles.

The two families are disjoint, so the total is 3 + 4 = 7.

CHOICE: 3
